title: spec review: Q5: orchestrator/planner_scorecard.py + `scorecard --planner-routing` — Planner outcomes by model × decision type × band × class × architectural, non-inferiority evidence per class, economics (P7, P13, P16)
spec:
Why: no code joins Planner invocations to downstream engineering outcomes; premium_summary (planner_runs.py:843) counts launches and tokens only. The router (Q4) needs class_evidence and the brief (P7/P13/P16) needs a Planner scorecard with cold-start priors and a CLI.
What: new module orchestrator/planner_scorecard.py plus cli.py flag `scorecard --planner-routing [--json]`.
- Inputs: invocation rows from schedlog.read("planner_invocations") merged by launch_id (later phases override; rows: launch_id, goal_id, decision_type, model, tier, band, task_class, architectural, started_at, material, reescalation, total_tokens, usd, latency_s, outcome), skip rows, bus tasks (root/tasks/*.json) and spec_review/review tasks. Tolerate missing files and malformed lines (count them in card["malformed"]).
- Attribution window: an invocation owns the goal's execute tasks whose lineage root (attribution.lineage) was created at or after started_at and before the goal's next invocation started_at; fix rounds count toward the root's owning invocation. A held-kind invocation also owns the fix-round task whose constraints.fix_round_for is that held task.
- group_key(row) -> "model|decision_type|band|task_class|arch" (arch = 'arch' or 'plain').
- build(root=STATE, *, cfg=None, min_samples=None) -> {"groups": {key: metrics}, "n": total invocations, "malformed", "min_samples"}; metrics per group: n, material_rate, downstream_accepted_rate (owned roots with merged_into), first_pass_rate (owned roots with pipeline.lineage_fix_rounds == 0 or no fix-round children), fix_round_rate, avg_fix_rounds, gate_red_rate (pipeline.gate_reds > 0), review_request_changes_rate (reviews with inputs[0] in owned ids and verdict request_changes), spec_review_approval_rate, replanning_rate (a later architectural_replan invocation for the same goal), reescalation_rate (rows reescalation True), human_intervention_rate (goal has an interactive attribution row after started_at when planner_telemetry.interactive_by_goal is available; else None), tokens_mean, usd_mean, latency_mean, evidence "sufficient"|"insufficient" (n >= min_samples; default from [planner.routing].min_samples 20 or [promotion].min_samples).
- class_evidence(model, decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, *, root=STATE, cfg=None) -> {"n", "noninferior": True|False|None, "deltas": {metric: delta}, "reescalation_rate", "baseline_model"}: compares the group with the same class group for the escalation tier's model (cfg [models].planner; fall back to tier fable rows). Non-inferior when both groups have n >= min_samples and first_pass_rate delta >= -0.02, avg_fix_rounds delta <= 0.05, gate_success (1 - gate_red_rate) delta >= -0.02, review_request_changes_rate delta <= 0.10, reescalation_rate <= 0.2 (thresholds from promotion.CRITERIA where names match, overridable under [promotion]); None when either side is insufficient; False when any threshold fails. Tokens, usd and latency never enter the verdict (docstring + test).
- economics(root=STATE) -> per model {"planner_usd_per_accepted_goal", "planner_tokens_per_accepted_goal", "pipeline_usd_after_planning" (sum of scorecard.by_task usd for owned tasks per invocation, mean), "expected_total_cost_after_planning" by decision_type (mean of planner usd + pipeline usd)}; accepted goals via scorecard.accepted_goals.
- format(card) -> text table sorted by key; format_evidence(evidence) one line. cli.py: `sc.add_argument("--planner-routing", action="store_true")`, dispatch to planner_scorecard.build/format (json with --json), conflict message with --planner like the existing --parallelism/--planner pair.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_groups_by_model_type_band_class_arch — invocations for two models and two decision types produce four group keys with n, material_rate and downstream_accepted_rate from owned tasks in the attribution window

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_attribution_window_and_fix_rounds_follow_root — a root task created after invocation A and its fix round created after invocation B both count toward A; a held-kind invocation owns the fix round with fix_round_for

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_class_evidence_noninferior_equivalent_worse_and_insufficient — opus equal to fable gives noninferior True; opus with first_pass 0.3 lower gives False with the failing delta named; n below min_samples gives None; a group with 1e9 tokens and 0 usd changes no verdict
tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_reescalation_penalises_class — reescalation_rate 0.5 on an otherwise equal class gives noninferior False with reason reescalation

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_cli_flag_and_malformed_tolerance — `scorecard --planner-routing --json` prints a card with groups and malformed count for a runs dir containing one malformed line; text output lists group keys

risks.issue: Sole input source schedlog stream "planner_invocations" has no producer anywhere in the codebase (verified via grep for planner_invocations, decision_type, architectural_replan). Scope/depends_on don't add an emitter. build() will tolerate the missing file and silently return n=0 forever in production, while synthetic-fixture unit tests pass, masking that the feature is disconnected end-to-end.

Spec's default path "[planner.routing].min_samples" names a nonexistent table; the real table is [planner.routes] and it has no min_samples key. The config override this spec promises can never actually be set.

class_evidence's claim that thresholds come "from promotion.CRITERIA where names match" is false as written — CRITERIA's keys (first_pass_delta, fix_rounds_delta, gate_success_delta, review_findings_delta) don't textually match the spec's own metric names (first_pass_rate, avg_fix_rounds, gate_success, review_request_changes_rate). The mapping is left to implementer guesswork and could diverge from promotion.py's semantics for what should be one shared criteria set.

planner_telemetry module doesn't exist at all (not just interactive_by_goal). Spec should explicitly require guarding the import itself (ImportError), not just a missing attribute, or the CLI will hard-crash instead of degrading human_intervention_rate to None.

suggested_spec_changes: Add a companion task (in scope or as an explicit depends_on) that emits schedlog.append("planner_invocations", row) at the real Planner-invocation call sites, and name where launch_id/decision_type/band/task_class/architectural actually originate today (they don't exist as concepts anywhere currently) — or explicitly scope this packet as read-side-only groundwork and say so in acceptance criteria so reviewers don't expect a populated scorecard post-merge.

Replace "[planner.routing].min_samples" with the config path that actually exists — either add min_samples under [planner.routes] in pool.toml as part of this task's scope, or drop the planner.routing fallback entirely and default straight from [promotion].min_samples.

Spell out the explicit metric-name -> promotion.CRITERIA-key mapping (e.g. a literal dict) instead of "where names match", so class_evidence and promotion.py can't silently diverge on the same non-inferiority definition.
Require the planner_telemetry lookup to be wrapped in try/except ImportError (not just missing-attribute handling), since the module doesn't exist in the repo yet.
